results.statement: sc-lint's SCB-MANIFEST-004 check must not report a self::X, crate::X or super::X path, in a use declaration or anywhere else in the code, as a use of the owned crate X, nor a bare X:: path in a module that declares its own mod X.
results.quote:
Issue #136 (atm-core, 2026-10-30): "`mod.rs:11` is `pub mod cron;` (file `commands/cron.rs`), and `crates/atm/Cargo.toml` has no `cron` dependency, so nothing imports the cron crate: it is **not a true violation and should not be reported**. [...] in a scratch file with no external dependency, 0.8.2 flags `use self::cron::X;`, `use crate::cron::X;` and `use super::cron::X;`, i.e. it matches the first path segment textually and does not distinguish a local module from the extern crate."

REQ-SCB-019 (docs/sc-lint-boundary/requirements.md): "Manifest findings use `SCB-MANIFEST-003` for a disallowed configured dependency, `-004` for a configured ownership violation, [...]"

criteria.no: The item is about a different rule or activity, for example PORT-010, SCB-MANIFEST-003 or other Cargo.toml dependency-table handling, lint step configuration, or release work, and does not touch how SCB-MANIFEST-004 classifies source paths.
criteria.unclear: The item mentions sc-lint-boundary or manifest rules, but it is not possible to tell whether it touches how SCB-MANIFEST-004 classifies source paths.
criteria.yes: The item changes, keeps, or depends on SCB-MANIFEST-004's decision about whether a source path (use statements, self::, crate:: or super:: paths, extern crate, ::name or bare crate paths) is a use of an owned dependency, including any plan to resolve atm-core #136 for that check, whether by code, configuration or documentation.

relevant.instructions: Does `item.text` plan, change, or depend on how the SCB-MANIFEST-004 check (also called global_dependency_ownership or the dependency-ownership rule, in crates/sc-lint-boundary) decides that a path in Rust source is a use of an owned dependency? Judge overlap of subject matter only. Do not judge whether the item obeys `anchor.statement`.

criteria.no: The item does not state that outcome: it is silent about these paths, covers only one or two of the three prefixes, only names issue #136 or improving path handling without saying these paths stop being reported, says they keep being reported, or is about another rule.
criteria.unclear: The item talks about how self::, crate:: or super:: paths are treated, but it cannot be determined whether local-module paths with all three prefixes stop being reported.
criteria.yes: The item states that self::, crate:: and super:: paths whose next segment is a local module (or all such qualified paths) are not reported by SCB-MANIFEST-004, using words such as skips, no finding, not reported, not counted as a use of the crate, or resolved to the local module instead of the owned crate.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` state that SCB-MANIFEST-004 will not report a path beginning with self::, crate:: or super:: as a use of an owned crate when the segment after the prefix is a local module of the crate? All three prefixes must be covered, either named or by a rule that applies to all qualified paths. Judge presence of this outcome only; do not judge conflict.

criteria.no: The item does not make or keep such paths reported; it fixes them, is silent, or concerns something else.
criteria.unclear: It is not possible to tell from the item whether such paths would stay reported.
criteria.yes: The item says such paths are or stay reported, or explicitly keeps the current matching unchanged.

contradicted.instructions: Would carrying out `item.text` leave SCB-MANIFEST-004 reporting a self::X, crate::X or super::X path as a use of owned crate X when X is a local module, because the item says so or explicitly keeps the current matching unchanged? Silence is not a conflict. Judge conflict only.
